title: UK GDP quarterly national accounts, Jul-Sep 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the December edition: a triple ONS stack with the Q3 balance of payments and November borrowing, and the thinnest payload of the four
source: EST: two publisher primaries fetched direct 2026-09-10, both HTTP 200. (1) ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpquarterlynationalaccountsukjulytoseptember2026 (42,204 bytes) reads verbatim 'GDP quarterly national accounts, UK: July to September 2026', 'Release date: 22 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published'. (2) The SAME release's machine-readable endpoint, ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpquarterlynationalaccountsukjulytoseptember2026/data, returns the publisher's own date-firmness flags: "release_date": "2026-12-22T07:00:00.000Z", "finalised": true, "provisional_date": "", "cancelled": false, "published": false, "national_statistic": true. That flag DISCRIMINATES rather than always reading true — the same endpoint returns "finalised": false for uknationalaccountsthebluebook2026 (2026-10-30), which is why this lane trusts it. Cadence scraped direct from four pages of the ONS's own past-release listing (HTTP 200 each, 40 editions 2016-09-30 -> 2026-06-30): the December edition ran on the LAST FRIDAY BEFORE CHRISTMAS for 2016-2019 (23 Dec 2016, 22 Dec 2017, 21 Dec 2018, 20 Dec 2019, all Fridays) and then switched, for six consecutive years 2020-2025, to a FIXED 22 December moved to the next working day when the 22nd falls on a weekend (22 Dec 2020 Tue, 22 Dec 2021 Wed, 22 Dec 2022 Thu, 22 Dec 2023 Fri, 23 Dec 2024 after the 22nd fell on a Sunday, 22 Dec 2025 Mon). 2026-12-22 is a Tuesday and a working day, so the modern rule predicts it exactly; the superseded pre-2020 rule would have said Friday 18 December, and the publisher's own page settles which applies. Filed estimate on the two counts every ONS entry on this calendar carries: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH OF THIS EVENT, 2026-09-10, after reading the one prior proposal (from-uk-quarterly-national-accounts-2026-09-30) in full. The proposal asked for exactly one thing — an out-of-sample re-run of its December identification — and this lane ran the tighter control it did not have. RESULT: the seasonality objection is REFUTED, not merely survived. A pre-Christmas-only control (15-24 December, non-QNA, n = 60) is NOT a quiet window at all — IGLT.L 1.02x an ordinary day (t = 0.13), FTSE 0.99x (t = -0.06), SPY 1.01x — while the ten December QNA days run IGLT.L 0.60x that same control (t = -2.46) and FTSE 0.36x (t = -4.52). The quiet belongs to the release day, not to December. Retitled on a second finding the proposal did not have: 07:00 on 2026-12-22 is a TRIPLE ONS stack — this release, the Q3 balance of payments and November public sector finances all print the same minute (each verified from its own release page and /data endpoint, HTTP 200, 2026-09-10) — and the co-print subset is the NOISY one, not the quiet one: the three historical QNA+PSF mornings (2018-12-21, 2019-12-20, 2020-12-22) moved IGLT.L 0.385% mean against 0.180% for the seven solo December editions, 2.14x (t = 1.92, n = 3). 2026-12-22 is the fourth such morning and the first since 2020. Tiered LOW on this lane's own measurement and on symbols: []: no December QNA day in ten years has exceeded the p90 of IGLT.L's ordinary days (max 0.581% on 2018-12-21 vs p90 0.809%), this repo tracks no UK-listed name, and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
